gamma_ray.built_from: OutSystems's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)

configs.what: OutSystems Agent Workbench with its documented defaults.
The builder places the agent in an ODC workflow with a Human activity assigned to a user or role; not part of an agent by default.
Agent guardrails enabled by an administrator (stage baseline) or a developer (per agent) in the ODC Portal; usage is charged through Agent Workbench add-on packs; not enforced in two regions.
The builder chains several agents as automatic activities in an ODC workflow (sequential, parallel or loop); not part of a single agent by default.
An administrator creates an A2A connection to an external agent in the ODC Portal and the builder adds its SendMessage action to the agent; ODC acts as A2A 0.3.0 client only.
An administrator creates a connection to an MCP server in the ODC Portal and imports selected tools as server actions, which the builder adds to the agent; not part of an agent by default.

facts.label: It works across several domains or systems
facts.fact: The product FAQ says agents connect to APIs, databases, ERP, CRM and legacy systems and orchestrate workflows across platforms.
facts.quote: Agents orchestrate workflows across platforms while maintaining security and governance.

facts.label: Several agents coordinate inside the organisation
facts.fact: Workflows chain several agents, each with its own lifecycle, passing one agent's output to the next.
facts.quote: With this pattern, you can chain multiple agents together sequentially.

facts.label: Agents operate across organisational boundaries or disparate stacks
facts.fact: Agentic apps can delegate tasks to external agents, outside ODC, over the A2A protocol.
facts.quote: allows your ODC agentic apps to interact and collaborate with external agents

facts.label: The agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only
facts.fact: In a workflow, agents run as automatic activities completed without human intervention, and a Human activity assigned to a user or role pauses the workflow until that person approves or rejects the agent's output.
facts.quote: allowing the workflow to resume based on the human's decision

facts.label: There is a published protocol or communication layer between agents
facts.fact: The A2A connector implements version 0.3.0 of the published Agent2Agent protocol, reading the remote agent card.
facts.quote: ODC A2A connector supports only A2A 0.3.0 protocol version

facts.label: It asks for narrower access than the whole account
facts.fact: The builder grants each agent a set of server actions it may call; with none granted, the agent relies only on the AI model's knowledge.
facts.quote: You provide the agent with a set of available actions.

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: The human-in-the-loop pattern stops at a high-stakes trigger until a person verifies or decides.
facts.quote: alerts a human user to provide verification or a decision before proceeding

facts.label: Its limits and known failure cases are documented for those who use it
facts.fact: The guardrails page documents where guardrails do not apply: files, some languages in basic-coverage regions, and two unsupported regions.
facts.quote: Prompts or responses in other languages can bypass safety filters.

facts.label: The data it uses is described
facts.fact: The docs describe agent grounding data: internal aggregates, search services and external tools.
facts.quote: Sources can include internal aggregates, search services (RAG), or external tools.

facts.label: The models and third-party components it uses are listed
facts.fact: The docs list the supported model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Gemini and others) and the trial models.
facts.quote: ODC supports connections to AI models from multiple providers

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of OutSystems's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
